Context/Background:
Intraductal papillary neoplasms (IPNs),  including intraductal papillary mucinous neoplasms (IPMNs), intraductal oncocytic papillary neoplasms (IOPNs), and intraductal tubulopapillary neoplasms (ITPNs), are clinically detectable macroscopic non-invasive cyst-forming lesions, some of which progress to invasive pancreatic cancer. Proteins and glycoproteins have proven to be useful clinical biomarkers for classifying cyst-forming neoplasms in the pancreas.Here, we used proteomics and glycoproteomics to characterize a series of histologically and genetically well-characterized surgically resected IPNs, including IPMNs and IOPNs.

Our analysis included 69 IPNs (64 IPMNs and 5 IOPNs), 76 macro-dissected grossly normal duct tissues (NDs, with 32 of the 76 NDs coming from the same resection specimens as the IPNs), and 32 cyst fluid samples (22 from matched IPMN patients, 3 matched IOPN patients, 2 from unrelated IPMN patients, and 5 other cysts).
Prompt: We applied proteomics-based NMF subtyping strategies to the IPMNs and PDACs to explore tumor heterogeneities and reveal progression features. This analysis showed three clusters, NMF 1 was entirely composed of PDACs. NMF 2 included some PDACs and some IPMNs, while NMF 3 was almost entirely composed of IPMNs with only one PDAC. Most (75%) IPMNs with an associated PDAC were clustered in NMF 2. Use the feature genes in each of the NMF clusters and pairwise comparison between clusters to interpret the differences between NMF clusters and provide a summary of functional and clinical implications.

Introduction/Context  
In resected pancreatic intraductal papillary neoplasms (IPNs; n = 69 IPMNs + IOPNs) and pancreatic ductal adenocarcinomas (PDACs), proteomics‐based non‐negative matrix factorization (NMF) identified three clusters (Wang et al., 2025). NMF 1 comprises exclusively PDACs, NMF 3 is almost entirely IPMNs, and NMF 2 a mix (75% of IPMNs with adjacent PDAC cluster here). Feature lists (Table S4G) and pairwise differential proteins (Table S4H) were analyzed via GSEA and ORA to reveal cluster‐specific biology. Tissue: surgically resected pancreatic lesions. Assay: quantitative proteomics. Dataset: Wang_2025_Cancer_Cell.

Keywords

• complement/coagulation  
• mitochondrial metabolism  
• ECM organization  
• translation/RNA processing

Analysis  
Cluster 3 (IPMN‐like) shows marked upregulation of secretory/exocytosis pathways (pancreatic and salivary secretion; RAB27B, SLC12A2, ATP1B1, RAB3D) and mitochondrial cristae formation (ATP5MG, ATP5ME), alongside downregulation of complement/coagulation cascades (C3, SERPINA1, CFB, CFH) and innate immunity. Cluster 2 (mixed IPMN/PDAC) is enriched in ECM‐receptor, PI3K‐Akt signaling, oxidative stress catabolism (HBD, MPO), heme metabolism, and EMT, with suppression of ribosomal RNA processing. Cluster 1 (PDAC) is balanced between developmental biology and core metabolism. These patterns delineate a progression axis from secretory, immune‐evading IPMNs (cluster 3), through ECM remodeling/stress‐adapted intermediate lesions (cluster 2), to proliferative PDACs (cluster 1).

Targeted (keyword-guided) subset  
Focusing on “secretion” terms in NMF 3 vs 1 (KEGG_2016): Pancreatic secretion (p = 0.027; RAB27B,SLC12A2,ATP1B1,RAB3D) and Salivary secretion (p = 0.033; LYZ,SLC12A2,ATP1B1). No other secretion‐related entries at FDR < 0.05, highlighting exocytic phenotype in IPMN‐like cluster.

Key Genes/Proteins (leading edge)  

Up  
| Gene     | Direction | Role/Function           | Pathway(s)                               |  
|----------|-----------|-------------------------|------------------------------------------|  
| RAB27B   | Up        | Vesicle trafficking     | Pancreatic secretion; Exocytosis         |  
| SLC12A2  | Up        | Ion transport           | Pancreatic secretion; Nitrogen transport |  
| HBD      | Up        | Oxygen transport/heme   | Heme metabolism; Oxidative catabolism    |  
| COL4A1   | Up        | ECM structural protein  | ECM‐receptor; EMT                        |  

Down  
| Gene      | Direction | Role/Function      | Pathway(s)                         |  
|-----------|-----------|--------------------|------------------------------------|  
| C3        | Down      | Complement effector| Complement cascade; Coagulation    |  
| DKC1      | Down      | rRNA pseudouridylase| rRNA processing; Gene expression   |  
| COQ6      | Down      | CoQ biosynthesis   | Core metabolism                    |  

Comparisons  
Secretory machinery (cluster 3) and ECM remodeling (cluster 2) share few leading genes, indicating distinct modalities. Mitochondrial‐ECM overlap in cluster 2/3 (e.g., ATP5MG, COX7A2L) suggests metabolic reprogramming at intermediate stages. Ribosomal suppression in cluster 2 vs cluster 1 aligns with slower proliferation in mixed lesions. Single-modality signals (e.g., complement loss only in cluster 3) warrant lower confidence outside IPMN context.

Implications  
Cluster 3’s secretory signature and immune evasion suggest biomarkers for early IPMN detection and stratification. Cluster 2’s ECM/oxidative stress module may underlie stromal remodeling and resistance; targeting PI3K‐Akt signals could intercept progression. Cluster 1’s developmental biology hallmarks point to stem‐like PDAC traits amenable to differentiation therapies.

Next Steps & Clarification  
1. Validate RAB27B‐mediated exocytosis in IPMN cyst fluid as noninvasive biomarker.  
2. Assess complement protein levels in NDs vs IPMNs for immune-editing insights.  
3. Test PI3K‐Akt inhibitors in organoid models of cluster 2 lesions.  
4. Confirm ribosomal suppression effects on proliferation in mixed IPMN/PDAC samples.  

References

2. Molecular Pathway and Immune Profile Analysis of IPMN-Derived Versus PanIN-Derived Pancreatic Ductal Adenocarcinomas. PMC11642437  
3. PubMed trend analysis for “mitochondrial metabolism IPMN”. PMID:40268349
